spans.s:
Anyataḥ-plakṣā (‘with wave-leafed fig-trees on one side only’) is the name of a lake in kurukṣetra according to the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, where it occurs in the story of purūravas and Urvaśī. Pischel places it somewhere in Sirmor.
Foot notes xi. 5, 1, 4.
Vedische Studien, 2, 217.

Anya-vāpa (‘sowing for others’).--The cuckoo is so called from its habit of depositing its eggs in the nests of other birds
Foot notes Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxiv. 37; Maitrāyaṇī Saṃhitā, iii. 14, 18.
